columns_doc.annualized_mint_rate: minted_next_boundary_near * 31536000 / (supply_start_near * epoch_seconds). Caveat: before protocol 45 nearcore sized the epoch reward by block count, not time (supply * max_inflation_rate * epoch_length / num_blocks_per_year; ProtocolFeature::RectifyInflation => 45 switched it to epoch_duration / num_seconds_per_year; nearcore 1.20.0 chain/epoch_manager/src/reward_calculator.rs and core/primitives/src/version.rs). In those epochs this time-based rate can exceed max_inflation_rate when blocks came faster than 1 per second; do not read it as the configured inflation rate there. mint_rate_above_max_inflation_rate lists the rows where it does.
columns_doc.burnt_in_block(b): sum(chunk.balance_burnt for chunks of block b with height_included == b.height); nearcore Block::produce sets supply(b) = supply(parent) + mint - this sum
columns_doc.burnt_in_epoch_near: fees burnt by blocks start..end = supply(start) - supply(end) + burnt_in_block(start). Inside an epoch supply only falls, by exactly each block's burn; the start block's supply delta also holds the mint, so its burn is read from its chunks instead. Supply-based, so it is the net burn after any gas rebate paid to contracts (burnt_gas_reward, 0.3 until protocol 87).
columns_doc.epoch_seconds: timestamp(end) - timestamp(last block of E-1): the duration nearcore pays for at next_start (as epoch_mints.epoch_seconds)
columns_doc.minted_next_boundary_near: supply(next_start) - supply(end) + burnt_in_block(next_start): the mint paid at E+1's first block for epoch E (as epoch_mints.minted_near)
columns_doc.protocol_version / max_inflation_rate: copied from the history_samples row (config at the sample height, inside E; protocol version is fixed per epoch)
columns_doc.start_height / end_height: first / last block of E; next_start_height = first block of E+1
columns_doc.supply_start_near: total_supply of the start block (after the mint for E-1 and the start block's own burn)

description: One complete epoch per history_samples target date (the epoch containing the 00:00 UTC sample block): its bounds, duration, supply, the mint paid for it and the fees burnt during it.
incremental_rule: Rows are immutable once written; only samples without a row are computed. Samples whose epoch has not ended by the tip are skipped and tried again next run.
method: last block of E-1 = block(header.next_epoch_id of the sample block); start = the next block (parent hash checked). end = block(header.next_epoch_id of the block at start + epoch_length, which is in E+1); next_start = the block after end (parent hash checked). Bisection on header.epoch_id is the fallback when a hash lookup does not land in the expected epoch. start_height is cross-checked against `validators` {block_id: end_height}.epoch_start_height where the node has it (Mar 2021+).
sampling: Epoch E = the epoch of the history_samples block for sample_date. Rows exist only for epochs that ended (next epoch's first block exists) by the tip of the run that wrote them.
